notes.meaning: Paul begins to pray for his readers, but he stops himself to mention his current situation. He is held in chains under Roman guard because he preached the message of Jesus to Gentiles, who are people not of Jewish heritage. Even though he is in prison, Paul sees himself as belonging to Christ and suffering for the good of other believers.
Paul assumes his readers already know about the special task God gave him. God gave Paul a generous gift of grace and chose him as an official servant to carry the good news to non-Jewish nations.

Paul explains that his message did not come from human teachers or his own study. God made known this truth directly to him through personal revelation, uncovering a plan that had stayed hidden for a long time.
Paul points out that anyone who reads what he has written can see the insight God gave him. Reading this letter allows believers to grasp his clear understanding of God's plan centered on Jesus.

In past generations, God did not make this secret plan clearly known to human beings. Now, through the Holy Spirit, God has fully revealed this truth to Christ's apostles and early Christian prophets.

The secret truth is that non-Jewish believers share fully with Jewish believers in all of God's blessings. By believing the good news about Jesus, Gentiles are equal members of the same spiritual body and receive the same Holy Spirit promised by God.

differ.view: The church is a completely new creation where earthly distinctions between Israel and Gentiles disappear into one spiritual body.
Gentiles are joined into the one continuing covenant people of God to share the promises originally given to Abraham.

notes.meaning: Paul explains that he became a servant of this good news only by God's free and unearned favor. This calling was not earned by Paul's own power or background, but was produced by the mighty working of God's power in his life.

Paul considers himself the least deserving of all God's holy people because he had hunted down and hurt Christians in the past. Even so, God gave him the wonderful task of telling the Gentiles about the endless, unfathomable riches found in Christ.
Paul was called to shine bright light on how God's hidden plan works out for everyone to see. This rescue plan had stayed hidden for ages in the heart of God, who created all things.

God intended to use the church to display His rich, many-sided wisdom to spiritual rulers in the heavenly places. As angels watch God bring people from every nation together in Christ, they see how wonderfully God fulfills His plans.
This gathering of believers was not an afterthought, but God's eternal plan made before the universe began. God has now carried out and completed this purpose through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Because believers are united to Jesus and trust in Him, they can enter God's presence freely. We do not have to approach God with terror, but can speak to Him with openness and joyful confidence.

Paul asks the believers not to lose heart or give up just because he is suffering in prison. His trials came from bringing them the gospel, so his steady faith brings honor and encouragement to their own Christian walk.
Paul returns to the prayer that he started earlier in the chapter. He falls on his knees before God the Father in deep humility and heartfelt worship.
God is the true Father who gives life and meaning to every family group in heaven and on earth. Every group of angels and humans depends on Him as their creator and caring head.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read it as 'every family.' Every family group, of angels in heaven and people on earth, gets the name 'family' from God the Father.

notes.meaning: Paul prays that God will draw from His limitless, glorious riches to give believers deep spiritual power. God provides this strength through the Holy Spirit working inside a person's heart and mind so they can stay faithful during hard times.

Paul asks that Christ will make His permanent home in their hearts as they continue to trust Him. When believers are firmly anchored like a tree with deep roots, and established like a building on a rock-solid base of love, their faith will not be shaken.

Paul wants all believers together to have the spiritual strength to understand the huge dimensions of Christ's love. This love extends wide enough to reach all people, long enough to last forever, deep enough to rescue the lost, and high enough to bring them to glory.

Paul prays that believers will personally experience Christ's love, even though it is far too great for any human mind to fully understand. Experiencing this love leads believers to be filled with all the spiritual life and goodness that God gives.

differ.view: Being filled with all the fullness of God describes Christian perfection, where a believer is filled with holy love far beyond mere pardon from sin.
Being filled with God's fullness describes the continuous growth of believers in spiritual gifts and grace throughout life.

notes.meaning: Paul closes with high praise to God, whose power has no limits. God is able to accomplish far beyond anything we could ever ask in prayer or imagine in our thoughts, using the mighty power that is already at work within us.
Paul proclaims that God deserves all honor and praise within the church and through Christ Jesus. This worship belongs to Him in every generation on earth and will never end throughout eternity.
